newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria bans banks' refinancing through reserves.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria bans banks' refinancing through reserves.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) decided on Wednesday to ban commercial banks from using their minimum reserves for emergency refinancing in what dealers said was a bid to relieve pressure on the slumping lev.
"The BNB board decided to suspend temporarily the use of the minimum required reserves by commercial banks, in force from January 30," a BNB statement said.
Though dealers said the decision would probably give the lev short-term relief, it more certainly would disturb interbank settlement payments.
So far, local commercial banks have been allowed to use daily up to 30 percent of their minimum required reserves at the central bank for emergency refinancing.
BNB officials were not available for comment.
The lev fell to a record low 1,300-1,450 per dollar at the Wednesday's close from 935-950 on Monday. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
